messages:
ivy: Noticed p95 on /v1/generate (prod-us) jumped ~160ms right after we reweighted traffic. No deploy at that time. Screenshot: https://console.redwood/snap-2025.png
marco: Probably composition effect. We merge per-route tdigests at endpoint-level. Changing weights can move aggregate percentiles even if both routes stayed identical.
tasha: This is causing churn in the SRE channel alerts are firing because our SLOs are bound to endpoint p95. We need a mitigation in the console and a short-term API option.
dane: Quick mitigation: show a subtle banner on endpoint pages: "Percentiles aggregated across routes. Routing or quota changes may shift these values." plus a small "breakdown" toggle. Also add a link "why did p95 change?" that explains t-digest merges at a high level.
ui-bot: UI mock: small origin-pill -> "sources: dedicated 67% | hosted 33%"; on click flip charts to per-route p50/p95/p99. Tooltip: "Aggregated via sketch-merge; use conservative mode for SLOs."
marco: API short-term: add `merge_mode` param with values `sketch-merge` (default), `per-route-weighted`, `per-route-max` and `include_provenance=true` to return counts per route. Backwards compatible because default remains sketch-merge.
tasha: For alerting: recommend route-level SLOs or `merge_mode=per-route-max` for conservative alarms. I'll update runbook and disable one noisy pager for the incident.
dane: Also add telemetry annotations when a quota-triggered reroute happens: emit event `reroute.reason=quota` so console can show timeline flags that line up with p95 shifts.
metrics-bot: metric-alert: p95 threshold exceeded for /v1/generate (prod-us) at 2025-06-22T14:12:08Z.
ivy: Owners: ivy -> incident note + runbook update, marco -> API RFC + impl, tasha -> alerting tests + SLO guidance, dane -> UI pill + explanation modal. Can we land a console canary and API flag behind a toggle in next deploy?
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: console-provenance-canary -> 2025-06-23T02:00:00Z (includes origin-pill + breakdown toggle behind feature flag).
marco: I'll open RFC + example curl in #pr-links. Tests will include synthetic weight flips to ensure per-route p95s remain stable while endpoint p95 moves.
